imported_from: closet-builder (github tarengesell-glitch/closet-builder): docs/cabinetry-intelligence/ (hard-constraints.md, design-preferences.md, construction.md, drawings.md, decision-log.md, sessions/) and the design-related shop facts in docs/construction-strategy.md. Read 2026-11-07.
requested_by: Owner (Taren), 2026-11-07: "bring in all the cabinet design rules for layout, spacing, symmetry, design aesthetic, etc from the closet-builder repo".
caution: closet-builder was written for a closet business and a different shop (Biesse/PEANUT joinery). Its rules are carried over as CANDIDATES for this platform. Only rules marked "confirmed" have been confirmed for this shop. None is applied by the software yet: there are no design-rule checks until the AI draft and design-rule checks are built. Lengths are in inches.

statuses.confirmed: The owner has confirmed it for this platform (see docs/DECISIONS.md, with the date in the note).
statuses.candidate: Carried over from closet-builder. Not yet confirmed for this platform or this shop. Needs the owner's yes before the software uses it.
statuses.conflicts: Disagrees with something the owner decided for this platform. This platform's decision wins; kept here so the difference is visible.
statuses.declined: The owner said no. Kept so it is not carried over again; neither the AI designer nor the design tool uses it.

kinds.hard: No design may break it. Would block (spec: a shop may promote a rule to block; which block by default is open question S-6).
kinds.preference: What we usually want. Scored and traded off, never enforced as pass/fail.
kinds.principle: A broader idea for the AI draft and for reviewing a design. Not a single number.
kinds.front_rule: How doors, drawer fronts, fillers and ends look and are sized, as far as the design shows them.
kinds.rejected: The owner said no to it as a default.

rules.title: Runs never occupy the same floor
rules.says: Each run claims its length along the wall plus its depth and room for fronts and handles. No other run may enter that space. Facing runs in a galley too narrow for both are reported, not overlapped.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "However, keep in mind that corner cabinets will intersect each other. The tool wouldn't even allow it to be drawn otherwise"

rules.title: A run stays inside its wall
rules.says: A run is never longer than its wall allows. A room edit that shortens a wall shortens its runs, and the screen says so.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The tool should not even allow cabinets to ever run into walls, that's a physical impossibility. The tool wouldn't even allow it to be drawn otherwise"

rules.title: Boxes stand gable to gable
rules.says: In a row each cabinet starts exactly where the one before it ends. With the fillers and end panels, the cabinets fill the run exactly.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The tool wouldn't even allow it to be drawn otherwise"

rules.title: Dishwasher right beside the sink base
rules.says: The dishwasher and the sink base must touch. No filler or corner between them (the dishwasher drains into the sink's drain).
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-04: "A dishwasher always has to be immediately next to a sink cabinet." Answer to Q-007: "B".

here.note: Matches the rough layout (owner, 2026-11-06): placing a sink adds a dishwasher right beside it, and it moves with the sink.

rules.title: A cabinet over the fridge is centred on the fridge
rules.says: A cabinet over a fridge is perfectly centred on the fridge.
rules.applies_when: A cabinet sits over a fridge
rules.source: Owner dictation, 2026-10-04: "perfectly centered on the fridge. That is non-negotiable."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes. Owner, 2026-11-08 (chat): "These should also not be allowed to be drawn."

rules.title: Whatever is over a cooktop is centred on it
rules.says: A hood fan, millwork hood or cabinet over a cooktop or range is centred on it. When the space over it is left open, the uppers either side are sized so the gap between them is centred on the cooktop. The gap's width comes from the code and the installation manual (the stricter decides), not a fixed 2" a side.
rules.source: Owner dictation, 2026-10-04: "They all need to be perfectly centered over top of the cooktop or stove. That is non-negotiable."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes. Owner, 2026-11-08 (chat): "These should also not be allowed to be drawn."

rules.title: 30" clear above the cooking surface
rules.says: Combustible cabinetry above a cooktop or range is at least 30" above the cooking surface. The building code's reductions and its exemptions for hoods and microwaves are not verified.
rules.applies_when: Cabinetry above a cooktop or range, Manitoba
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-04, answer to Q-005: "30". Code reference (unverified): NBC 2020 Art. 9.10.22.2, M.R. 78/2023.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "Still applies to the visual tool, and to the measurements we'll send to CV via [the CAD import file]. The tool wouldn't even allow it to be drawn"

open: Read the code article itself to confirm 30" is at least what it requires.

rules.title: Protection of combustibles beside a cooktop
rules.says: From research, NOT VERIFIED: combustible finishes or cabinets within about 450 mm of the cooktop are protected above element level. No value is to be used until the code text is read.
rules.source: Owner dictation, 2026-10-04 (asked for the code setback as a rule). NBC Art. 9.10.22.3, unverified.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "Still applies to the visual tool, and to the measurements we'll send to CV via [the CAD import file]. The tool wouldn't even allow it to be drawn"

rules.title: Appliance and fixture specs confirmed before sign-off
rules.says: Placeholder appliances are fine while designing. Sign-off and sending to production wait until every appliance's and fixture's specs are confirmed and the cabinetry meets their installation requirements.

here.note: Same as the spec's push condition "appliances confirmed" (OA-5).

rules.title: Countertop into an appliance opening: at most 1/4", equal both sides
rules.says: Where a countertop ends at an appliance or fixture opening, it projects 0 to 1/4" from each side, never more, and the two sides are exactly equal. The usual 1" overhang does not apply there. Example: a 31" opening for a slide-in range gives a 30 1/2" counter opening.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes, with a change. "Consider the stone fabricator and the shop one and the same. This really only applies to Free standing ranges. It's a constraint that the tool wouldn't even allow to be drawn otherwise"

rules.title: Verified site measurements before sign-off
rules.says: A design may use preliminary measurements, and a quote may use the homeowner's or a blueprint's. Sign-off and production need verified site measurements, recording who verified them and when (us, a contractor, the designer or the homeowner).
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Final sign-off and sending to production should not be allowed without verified site measurements." Q-019: "We just have to confirm who and when."

here.note: Same as the spec's push condition "site measured" (OA-5). Who may verify is not yet decided here.

rules.title: Anything that opens opens without hitting anything
rules.says: Doors, drawers, roll-outs, corner hardware and appliance doors complete their movement without hitting cabinetry, handles, walls, appliances, room doors or each other. Handles count. No clearance distance is invented: it comes from the real hardware and appliance.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true. The tool wouldn't even allow it to be drawn"

rules.title: Known site conditions are constraints
rules.says: Walls, bump-outs, columns, doors, windows, soffits, plumbing, electrical, HVAC and hood ducts that affect fit or use are constraints when known.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes.

rules.title: Smallest cabinet widths
rules.says: By outside width: an upper at least 8"; a base with only doors at least 8"; a cabinet with drawers at least 12".

here.note: Confirmed in the library review, 2026-11-07 (DECISIONS).

rules.title: No cabinet wider than 42"
rules.says: A cabinet is never more than 42" wide. Up to 38" one cabinet is preferred to two (PREF-025).
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Not totally hard and firm. 42 is the hard and firm".

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Cabinets 24" to 32" wide
rules.says: When a run is divided into cabinets, make as many as possible 24" to 32" wide. The ideal for looks and for sheet yield.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-09-28 (shop fact 25); 2026-10-05: "24-32 box cases are ideal".

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Few cabinets over 36"
rules.says: As few cabinets as possible over 36" wide. Loses to PREF-025 up to 38".

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Avoid cabinets under 12"
rules.says: Avoid cabinets narrower than 12". An aim, not a limit (the limits are HARD-015).
rules.source: Owner, 2026-09-28 (shop fact 25); aim, not limit: answer to Q-035, 2026-10-05.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Fairly symmetrical runs
rules.says: Cabinet widths across a run look balanced, but cabinet size comes first: 80" of cabinets is 32 + 32 + 16, not three of 26 5/8. A 90" run is two 3/4" fillers and three 29 1/2" cabinets. ASSUMED order of trying (read from those examples): equal cabinets if they land in 24–32"; then full 32s plus one; then the most even split, wider ones at both ends; an odd one at the right end.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-09-28 (shop fact 25: "fairly symmetrical" and the two examples). The order of trying is assumed.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Shoe and boot shelf spacing
rules.says: Flat shoe shelves 8" apart, the first 7" up; boots 16".
rules.source: Owner accepted published closet guides, 2026-09-28 (shop fact 28).

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: A four-drawer bank near the sink and dishwasher
rules.says: A bank of four drawers should be close to the sink cabinet and dishwasher.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

open: How close is close? Is one bank enough?

rules.title: One or two four-drawer banks beside the cooktop
rules.says: At least one, ideally two, four-drawer banks for pots and pans right beside the cooking appliance. Closer is better. Drawers, not deep shelves behind doors.
rules.source: Owner dictation, 2026-10-04: "a very, very strong preference, but not a hard rule"; confirmed 2026-10-05.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Countertop overhangs 1"
rules.says: Counters overhang 1" past a finished end and 1" past the face of a door or drawer front. Not at an appliance opening (HARD-011).

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "Consider the stone fabricator and the shop one and the same."

rules.title: The cabinet over the fridge lines up with the fridge panel
rules.says: The cabinet over a fridge is deep enough that its door face is flush with the front of the fridge panel beside it.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Grain carries on across connected cabinets
rules.says: Where cabinets are connected, the grain carries on from one to the next. May lose to material yield and cost. Within one cabinet it is a rule (CON-005).
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "a bonus/strong preference, not a rule".

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: No.

rules.title: Walkways 42" to 48"
rules.says: Under 36": breaks a very strong minimum. 36" to 42": possible, below preferred. 42" to 48": preferred. Over 48": breaks a very strong maximum.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Islands line up with nearby runs
rules.says: Islands are sized and placed to line up with other runs. When an island's end is close to a wall run's end, they line up exactly ("like snapping").
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Islands should be sized and positioned to line up with other runs of cabinetry."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Fixtures roughly in line align exactly
rules.says: An island sink and a back-wall range that are roughly in line are lined up exactly.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: A roughly centred island fixture is centred exactly
rules.says: A sink or cooktop roughly centred on an island is centred exactly.
rules.strength: extremely strong, "almost a hard constraint", but not hard

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Solve the fixed things first, then share out the rest
rules.says: 1 set the run's ends; 2 set aside fillers and end panels; 3 lock confirmed appliance and fixture openings; 4 lock cabinets with deliberate widths; 5 share the remaining space; 6 recheck the total.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Acceptable cabinet widths 12" to 36"
rules.says: 12–36" is acceptable; 24–32" is ideal (PREF-001).

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Ideal door width 14" to 16"
rules.says: Each visible door: ideal 14–16"; backup 12–14" and 16–20". Drawer fronts have no ideal width (the cabinet width decides). A 30" two-door cabinet is judged on its two 14 7/8" doors.

here.note: "Ideal door 14–16"" confirmed in the library review, 2026-11-07 (DECISIONS). The backup bands are not yet confirmed here.

rules.title: Drawer and front lines carry across neighbours
rules.says: Lines between drawer fronts continue across neighbouring drawer banks, and prominent front lines (the top of a door and the drawer beside it) continue across neighbouring bases. Random changes score worse unless function or a deliberate composition explains them.

here.note: In part: the 6 13/16" top drawer lines up across cabinets (DECISIONS 2026-11-07).

rules.title: Equal widths either side of a focal point
rules.says: Around a range, hood, over-range cabinet, sink, major window, niche or feature cabinet, the two cabinets immediately either side are equal widths where function allows. 18 | 36 HOOD | 18 beats 15 | 36 HOOD | 21.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Consistent top and bottom lines; deliberate steps
rules.says: A tall cabinet beside uppers shares their top line. Uppers in one run keep a consistent top, bottom or crown line. Where heights change, the change looks deliberate (a hierarchy, a repeated step, a focal composition), not accidental.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Repeated widths make rhythm; random one-offs are penalised
rules.says: Within one area, use a small deliberate set of widths (not every cabinet equal). 24 | 30 | 24 | 30 | 24 beats 18 | 27 | 21 | 33 | 16 | 24. A width that function needs is never refused.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Correct; this should create a penalty."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Style decides how many divisions
rules.says: Calm or contemporary designs suit fewer, wider fronts. Traditional or detailed designs can suit more, smaller divisions.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes.

rules.title: Sink centred under a window; balance around a focal window
rules.says: When a sink and window are nearly aligned and function allows, the sink centres under the window. Cabinetry either side of a focal window is balanced. Local to the window; not every sink goes under every window.

here.note: The centring part is in the rough layout (owner, 2026-11-06): a sink dropped near a window centres under it, with a notice when it isn't.

rules.title: Narrow doors beside a cooktop or sink hinge away from it
rules.says: Narrow single-door cabinets right beside the cooktop or sink open away from it, because the cook stands there. In 28 | 14 | 36 | 14 | 28 the left 14 hinges left, the right 14 hinges right. Never overrides HARD-013.
rules.strength: very strong beside a cooktop or sink; a weaker bonus beside prep areas; not hard

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Up to 38", one cabinet beats two narrow ones
rules.says: Where the space could be one cabinet up to about 38" or two of half that, one is better. Beats PREF-002 up to 38". Never over 42" (HARD-016).
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Yes. up to 38" a single 38" box is preferential to two 19" boxes".

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Drawers rather than doors for everyday base storage
rules.says: Full-extension drawer bases are preferred to doors with shelves for kitchens, and vanities where plumbing allows. Except sinks, equipment, specialty cabinets, or where a door is genuinely better.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: A cutlery drawer and a separate utensil drawer
rules.says: One drawer for flatware with a cutlery insert, and a separate drawer for cooking utensils. Both by default in a full kitchen.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Very strong preference. Include both by default."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Cutlery and everyday dishes near the dishwasher
rules.says: What is put away from the dishwasher, above all cutlery, goes near the dishwasher and cleanup zone.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Vertical tray storage, over the fridge by default
rules.says: Vertical dividers for baking sheets, cutting boards and trays, by default in the cabinet over the fridge when it can hold them.
rules.strength: default; its place is a strong default

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Concealed garbage and recycling between sink and prep
rules.says: An integrated waste and recycling pull-out, placed to serve both prep and the sink.
rules.strength: default; its place is very strong

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Pull-outs inside tall pantry cabinets
rules.says: Tall pantry cabinets get internal pull-out drawers or trays rather than deep fixed shelves.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Organised spice storage by default
rules.says: A dedicated spice solution near the cooking zone. The system is undecided.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Yes, include it by default. We will need to select a default system."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: A proper corner mechanism whenever a corner holds storage
rules.says: No deep blind corner with fixed shelves. If a corner holds storage it gets an access mechanism (carousel, corner pull-out or similar). Leaving the corner empty can be better.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Vanity drawers shaped around the plumbing
rules.says: Notched or U-shaped drawers reclaim storage around vanity sink plumbing, where construction and the plumbing allow.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: No. "Forget about this for the visual tool. I'm not sure how we'll program this parametrically."

rules.title: Laundry room basics
rules.says: A folding surface (very strong); somewhere to hang or air-dry clothes (strong); laundry products stored by the machines (strong).

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Mudroom basics
rules.says: A bench with shoe storage (very strong); small-item storage for keys, gloves and mail (strong); exposed hooks (moderate, never at the cost of the design).

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: The recommended closet cabinet
rules.says: Top to bottom: a shelf over the hanging if there is room; open hanging with a rod; drawers at the bottom. Doors only if there is room to open them. A recommendation, not a rule.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: The stricter of the code and the installation manual decides
rules.says: When the building code and a manufacturer's installation manual give different clearances, follow the stricter.
rules.source: Owner dictation, 2026-10-04: "I want the stricter one to decide."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: The installation guide beats the spec sheet
rules.says: When an appliance's spec sheet and installation guide disagree, use the installation guide.
rules.source: Owner dictation, 2026-10-04: "go for the installation guide."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Clearances are measured from the finished outside
rules.says: Doors, fronts, finished panels, countertops, handles and appliances stand beyond the cabinet, so they decide the real clearance.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Fillers and panels are real parts
rules.says: Fillers and end panels are their own items with their own space, not space hidden in a cabinet width.

here.note: Fillers are their own catalog item here, cut to fit (DECISIONS 2026-11-07).

rules.title: Walkways against alignment and centring: no fixed order
rules.says: When walkway width and alignment or centring pull against each other, the AI suggests the trade-off and explains it, and the designer decides. Narrowed by PRIN-013 for lining up.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Near enough becomes exact
rules.says: When things that read as a pair or a shared line nearly match, close the gap. A small miss is worse than an exact match or a clearly deliberate offset. 17 7/8 | FOCAL | 18 1/8 becomes 18 | FOCAL | 18.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Align the edges that matter, not every seam
rules.says: Uppers and bases may use different widths; their ordinary seams needn't line up. Related edges (run ends, appliance, window and tall-cabinet edges) should. Three 24" uppers over two 36" bases is fine.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Some lines matter more than others
rules.says: Most important first: 1 focal appliance and hood centrelines; 2 window and sink axes; 3 the outer ends of a composition; 4 tall and upper top lines; 5 major drawer and front lines; 6 large panel and end lines; 7 ordinary seams.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Judge the visible fronts, not just the cabinets
rules.says: Equal cabinet widths aren't enough; the visible doors and drawer fronts should balance and repeat. 18 | 24 | 36 FOCAL | 24 | 18 is symmetrical in cabinets; 14 | 28 | 36 FOCAL | 28 | 14 is better; 28 | 14 | 36 FOCAL | 14 | 28 is preferred (every door 13 7/8").

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Symmetry is local; deliberate asymmetry is fine
rules.says: A room can hold several compositions (a symmetrical range wall, an asymmetrical sink wall, a symmetrical island). A wider element may set a hierarchy on purpose. Asymmetry from function or design is fine; unexplained near-pairs are not.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Function outranks decorative symmetry
rules.says: Don't chase symmetry at the cost of storage, appliance use, clearances, plumbing or the right cabinet type. Hard rules always win.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: Yes.

rules.title: Judge composition in elevation
rules.says: Front alignment, rhythm, heights and focal symmetry can only be judged in the wall (front) view, not the plan.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes.

rules.title: Lining up beats a wider walkway, but not below 36"
rules.says: When lining up and walkway width can't both be met, lining up wins as long as the walkway stays over 36".
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Lining up should win, while keeping a walkway larger than 36"".

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Store things where they're used, sized to what they hold
rules.says: Reason from the task to what is stored to where it goes: cookware by the cooktop, cutlery by the dishwasher, spices by the cooking, garbage by prep and cleanup. Never add an insert just to fill leftover space.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: What counts as a default
rules.says: A feature is in a basic design by default only if an experienced designer would be surprised to see it missing. Nice-to-haves are optional and never added automatically.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Separate the storage function from the product
rules.says: Rules name the function ("cutlery organisation", "corner access"); the catalog maps it to a product.
rules.source: Chat synthesis, 2026-10-05; not the owner's words.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Finished end at an open end, filler at a wall
rules.says: An applied end panel matching the doors goes on any cabinet end with no wall and no cabinet beside it. A filler goes at a wall end.

here.note: Same as this platform's ends decision (2026-11-07): Applied finished end at an open end by default, Unfinished with a filler at a wall.

rules.title: Door sizes and splits
rules.says: 1/16" from each outside edge; each door of a pair is 1/8" less than half the cabinet; one door up to 20" wide, then a pair; one door up to 48" tall, then two stacked. Under a countertop the door top is 1/4" down from the cabinet top; otherwise flush.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-09-26 (shop fact 16); 1/4" under a counter reconfirmed 2026-10-05.

here.note: Confirmed in the library review, 2026-11-07, except the 1/4" drop under a countertop, which is not yet confirmed here. Owner review, 2026-11-08: "Keep these measurements for drawing in the visual tool, but the shop's library is the authority: if its numbers differ, the library wins."

rules.title: Gaps between fronts are 1/8"
rules.says: 1/8" between a pair of doors, stacked doors and drawer fronts; with 1/16" at each outside edge, neighbouring cabinets' fronts are 1/8" apart too. Each cabinet's paired doors are equal width. Fronts that share a plane stay in it.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "Door gaps should always be 1/8""; paired doors equal and fronts in one plane: "Hard rule" (A-01, A-05, A-06).

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: No. "These are construction rules. We will not set our own construction rules in this tool, rather we will use the CV and shop construction rules"

rules.title: Shelves evenly spaced, no opening under 6"
rules.says: Adjustable shelves in a space are spaced evenly, and no opening between them may be less than 6".

here.note: "Shelves are evenly spaced" confirmed 2026-11-07. The 6" minimum opening is not yet confirmed here. Owner review, 2026-11-08: "Keep these measurements for drawing in the visual tool, but the shop's library is the authority: if its numbers differ, the library wins."

rules.title: Dividing a run into cabinets
rules.says: The run length is fixed. Each end gives up 3/4" to a filler (at a wall) or an applied finished end (open end). The rest is divided into cabinets by outside width on 1/16" steps, with the aims PREF-001 to PREF-004. Making one cabinet wider makes the others narrower.

here.note: The 1/16" width step and 3/4" fillers are confirmed here (2026-11-07). The splitting aims are candidates (see PREF-001 to PREF-004).

rules.title: Corners: the longest run takes the corner
rules.says: The longest run goes to the end of its wall; the run on the next wall stops about 10" short of its fronts, with an end panel. No corner cabinet.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: "This is only in relation to how opposing runs of closet cabinets should snap when dragging cabinet runs during the wall and cabinet layout drawing step". Kitchen corners still use corner cabinets (2026-11-06).

rules.applies_when: Closet cabinet runs facing each other, while a run is being dragged in the wall and cabinet layout step

rules.title: Toe kick 3 7/8" tall
rules.says: The standard toe kick is 3 7/8" tall everywhere (better yield from a 48" sheet).

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-07: No. "Use the toe kick height from the CV 11 library from the shop"

rules.title: Upgrade: 1 1/2" fillers and finished ends
rules.says: An optional room-wide upgrade makes every filler and finished end 1 1/2" thick (one sheet-good panel, not solid wood). Each such run end then sets aside 1 1/2" instead of 3/4".

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "This is a visual upgrade that our tool will have. We will map it to a construction rule in the CV shop library."

rules.title: Crown moulding sets the gap above the cabinets
rules.says: With a crown, the cabinet top is exactly the crown's size below the ceiling (height set from the ceiling down). With no crown, any height, but never closer than 1" to the ceiling. Placeholder crowns: 2", 3", 4", 5", 6".
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-06 (shop fact 48): "Cabinets will be spaced anywhere from 1-6" away from the ceiling depending on what crown mould is specified."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "Yes, this will be the case when we set a ceiling height + cabinets to ceiling + a crown selection."

rules.title: Fronts on one cabinet are grain-matched
rules.says: The fronts of one cabinet are always cut from grain-matched, continuous sections of the sheet, for every grained or patterned material. "Non-negotiable."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "Fronts in our visual tool should be grain matched. And yes the shop will set its cutlist to do this in CV."

rules.title: Stone countertop drawings show intent only
rules.says: The stone templater measures on site. Our countertop drawings show overall sizes, finished, unfinished and wall edges, and where fixtures and appliances go. They don't replace the field template.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes.

rules.title: Pot-lid organiser
rules.says: A dedicated pot-lid organiser is an optional upgrade, never added automatically.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Pull-out ironing board
rules.says: Useful but optional, never added automatically.

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

rules.title: Not defaults: vanity organiser drawer, hair-tool organiser, pull-out hamper, laundry sorting baskets
rules.says: None of these is added by default.
rules.source: Owner, 2026-10-05: "No" / "This doesn't require anything in our system."

here.note: Owner review, 2026-11-08: Yes. "The storage, kitchen and clearance rules are confirmed as true."

design_tool.how_used: Owner, 2026-11-07: the AI designer gets the confirmed rules, the room's walls and cabinet runs, and the client's intake preferences, and drafts the best-fit design and layout from them. The design_tool setting only matters in the design tool, when a designer's own change breaks a rule.
design_tool.not_drawable: The design tool won't let it be drawn (owner, 2026-11-08).
design_tool.error: Shown as an error the designer must fix.
design_tool.suggestion: Shown on the running list of design preferences that could be improved (owner, 2026-11-07). Every confirmed preference is here.
design_tool.none: Nothing to check in the design tool: guidance for the AI designer, or how the tool draws things.
design_tool.unset: A confirmed hard rule with no setting yet (design_tool left out).
